hints: The distance between u and v can be split at their lowest common ancestor.
analogy: Their paths go up to a shared ancestor and down again; subtract the shared climb counted twice.
example: If depths are 4 and 3 and the LCA depth is 1, distance is 4+3-2=5 edges.
algorithm: Precompute depth and binary-lifting ancestors. For each query compute LCA and apply the depth formula.
correctness: The unique tree path consists of u-to-LCA plus LCA-to-v; their lengths are depth[u]-depth[l] and depth[v]-depth[l].
complexity: O(n log n+q log n) time and O(n log n) space.
